Run a set of checks and collect the verdict

Source: R/gate.R
run_gate.Rd

An error inside a check does not stop the gate: it becomes a blocking CHECK_ERROR result, as in bdp-model-gate. That is right in production and is also why tests must assert values rather than that a check "ran" - see the run_gate_strict() helper in tests/testthat/helper-guard.R.

Usage

run_gate(context, checks = default_checks())

Arguments

context

A gate_context().

checks

List of new_check() objects. Defaults to default_checks().

Value

An object of class gate_report.

Details

A check that returns nothing, or anything other than a list of check_result()s, is also a CHECK_ERROR: a check that says nothing must not read as a check that found nothing.

Examples

set.seed(1)
X_train <- data.frame(age = rnorm(200, 40, 10), income = rlnorm(200, 10, 0.5))
X_val <- data.frame(age = rnorm(100, 40, 10), income = rlnorm(100, 10, 0.5))
report <- run_gate(gate_context(X_val, X_train = X_train,
                                model_card = list(use_case = "marketing",
                                                  validation_strategy = "random_split")))
report
#> <gate_report> status: PASS (0 finding(s) in 6 result(s))
as.data.frame(report)[, c("check_name", "flag")]
#>            check_name           flag
#> 1      target_leakage NOT_APPLICABLE
#> 2       split_overlap             OK
#> 3       split_overlap             OK
#> 4 validation_strategy             OK
#> 5    feature_contract             OK
#> 6       feature_drift             OK
